reason: While the text describes severe famine-induced suffering in Egypt, when the people cry out to Pharaoh for bread (וַיִּצְעַק הָעָם אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה לַלָּחֶם), Pharaoh's response is to direct them to Joseph for food provision (לְכוּ אֶל־ יוֹסֵף אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמַר לָכֶם תַּעֲשׂוּ), not to blame them for the suffering. No leader in this passage assigns fault to the people for the famine. Joseph had interpreted Pharaoh's dreams as God's revelation of coming events and prepared accordingly, but no blame is attributed to the suffering population.
